PASS: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 4 — ROUND 1 — VERDICT: PASS
Audited commit 08754c62fb91cf4910cb934df4686aecf5204e27 on main, against base 55301c8 (Sprint 3 ship record). Working tree clean; committed code.
Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. No cross-version ("arrives between release A and B") criterion in this sprint. No new dependencies. Dev Team 2 worktree confirmed removed (git worktree list shows main only).

This is fine. Every acceptance criterion verified directly, one sprint-file defect to hand back to Master Controller, and a short list of non-blocking follow-ups.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — all verified by me, not read off the tests ===
- Normalization triple: https://clientdomain.com/About/, http://www.clientdomain.com/about, https://staging.clientdomain.com/about/#team → all '/about'. Query-order normalization also confirmed (?b=2&a=1 == ?a=1&b=2). The www. fold is subsumed by dropping the host entirely — a strictly stronger transform, documented in normalize.js as requirement 3 demands.
- Pure comparison, no network: ran test/compare/*.test.js with dns.lookup/dns.promises.lookup/resolve4/6 and global fetch replaced by throwing stubs — 69/69 pass. compare.js imports nothing capable of I/O (grep-confirmed; compare.test.js:15 asserts it structurally too).
- Three groups: fixture with all three non-empty → onLiveOnly ['/a'], onStagingOnly ['/c'], onBothCount 1. Empty live → 0/1/0. Empty staging → 1/0/0. Both empty → no throw.
- Titles fetched ONLY for differing items — the performance criterion, verified by count: 500 on-both URLs + 1 live-only + 2 staging-only → exactly 3 outbound requests, onBothCount 500. The on-both set is never materialized as a list (only counted), so there is nothing to accidentally fetch.
- Fallback paths, asserted on the returned item: 404 → slug; 500ms response under a 50ms timeout → slug; application/pdf → slug; HTML with no <title> → slug (a case requirement 8 doesn't name but should). All 4 items retained. Each carries titleSource:'slug'; a real fetch carries 'fetched'.
- Slug: /news/q3-earnings/ → "Q3 Earnings"; /about_our_team/ → "About Our Team"; /blog/caf%C3%A9-guide/ → "Café Guide"; bare / → "Home" (fallback label, never empty).
- Suffix: " - Acme" and " | Acme" both stripped; "Well-known co-op results" untouched (no spaced separator); "Q3 - the good - the bad - Acme" untouched (separator appears more than once → deliberately conservative, per titleSuffix.js). This is the right bias: under-strip beats silently losing title content.
- titleSource present on every item; completeness passthrough: staging.truncated:true + 1 ambiguous → result.truncated:true, completeness.staging.truncated:true, ambiguous length 1. A truncated crawl cannot present as clean.
- Basic Auth sidedness: Authorization PRESENT on the staging-side title fetch, ABSENT on the live-side one — two guardedFetch instances, one with auth, one without, selected by item.side. This is tighter than requirement 7's wording and correct: staging credentials never go to the live host (which may sit behind a third-party edge).
- HTTP boundary (req 12): lib/compare/ requires no http/https/net/undici, constructs no Agent, reuses createGuardedFetch + createLimiter from lib/sitemap; imports nothing from src/db or src/lib/crypto. fetchImpl and dnsLookup injected exactly as Sprint 3's crawler does. Sprint 5's connection-pinning fix will therefore apply once.
- Carry-forward fixes (req 13/14), each demonstrated with captured outbound headers where relevant:
  H — same-host https→http redirect: hop 1 Authorization PRESENT, hop 2 (http) ABSENT. Same-host port change (→ :8443): ABSENT. Origin comparison, not hostname. This was the credential-downgrade leak; it is closed.
  G — exact-token exclusion: 'tagline-sitemap.xml' → ambiguous (was 'exclude' by prefix on 'tag'); 'tag-sitemap.xml' still exclude; 'post-sitemap2.xml' still include. See SPRINT FILE DEFECT below re: the requirement's own example.
  I — userinfo redaction: manualSitemapUrl 'https://user:s3cret@…' → error message, .url, .cause.message, and discovery attempts log all free of 's3cret'. Verified against Node 24's REAL fetch, not only the fake: raw fetch('https://user:s3cret@…') throws a TypeError whose message contains the secret; through createGuardedFetch the typed ConnectionError's util.inspect() output (what console.error would print, including .cause) does not. Dev Team's handoff claim on this is accurate.
  J — duplicate ambiguous: my Sprint 3 round-2 repro (child referenced by root directly and again via a delayed post-sitemap) → ambiguous lists it exactly once. ctx.ambiguousRecorded Set.
- npm test 324/324, npm run lint exit 0.

=== REQUIREMENT 5 — the one that extended Sprint 3, and the design ruling ===
Dev Team is right that Sprint 3's output never tagged individual URLs page-vs-post; classify.js decided include/exclude/ambiguous per sitemap only. The sprint file's "carrying through the source sitemap classification from Sprint 3" assumed a signal that didn't exist. Threading a sourceType through crawl.js's recursion is the correct place to add it — crawl.js is the only site that holds both "which sitemap" and "the URL" — and it was disclosed up front rather than discovered by me. Verified: page-sitemap.xml → 'page'; post-sitemap.xml → sitemap-1.xml (untyped intermediate) → 'post' (inherited); gallery-sitemap.xml under an untyped root → undefined (an honest unknown, never a guess).
RULING on inherit-down vs re-derive-per-level: inherit-down is correct. Keep it. The child's own filename wins when it names a type; the parent's type fills the gap only when the child's doesn't. Re-deriving independently at each level would return undefined at exactly the shape where the signal matters most (a typed index whose children are numbered sitemap-N.xml), and there is no shape where inheritance mis-labels: a typed child under a differently-typed parent takes its own type, and an untyped child under an untyped parent stays undefined. This is the design Sprint 5 should build its grouping on.

=== SPRINT FILE DEFECT — for Master Controller (raised here per the sprint-9 instruction, not absorbed) ===
Requirement 13(G) says "so a hypothetical products-guide-sitemap.xml is not silently excluded by product-". It is still excluded — correctly — because 'products' (plural) is itself an exact token in EXCLUDE_KEYWORDS, present since Sprint 3 for WooCommerce sitemaps. The example cannot demonstrate the fix; only a token that is a PREFIX of a keyword without being one ('tagline' vs 'tag', 'authority' vs 'author') can. The fix is real and demonstrated with 'tagline'; the requirement's example is the defect. Recommend amending the example in the sprint file so the record is accurate, or accept this note as the correction. Dev Team's test for req 14 correctly used a demonstrable case rather than the stated one — that is the right call, and it should be visible that it was a call.

=== NON-BLOCKING ===
K. [LOW, for Sprint 5's UI] The TechCrunch-style 'sitemap-page-N.xml' convention yields sourceType 'page', but on that site those are paginated POST sitemaps ("page" is pagination, not WP pages). The classifier can't know; it's doing what requirement 5 says. Sprint 5 should treat sourceType as "by sitemap name" and group softly — not present 'page' vs 'post' as ground truth.
L. [LOW] resolveTitles swallows the fetch error type (titleFetcher.js:93 `catch {}`) — the item records titleSource:'slug' but not WHY. A 401/403 on a staging title fetch means the saved credentials are wrong, which is the single most useful thing the UI could say; a timeout means something else. Carry err.code onto the item (e.g. titleError) so Sprint 5 can surface it. Requirement 9 as written is met.
M. [LOW] No overall budget across title resolution: 100 items / 5 concurrency × 10s timeout = 200s worst case on a slow staging host. Requirement 7 asks for per-request timeout + cap only, so this is met as written; Sprint 5's scan route will want an overall budget on the whole scan, and should set it there.
N. [LOW] titleSuffix: a title containing both separators once each ("Foo - Bar | Acme") strips at the first (' - '), yielding "Foo" and losing " - Bar". Counting all separator occurrences across both kinds before acting would keep the conservative bias consistent. Also: Yoast's separator options include en-dash and em-dash (" – ", " — "); requirement 6 names only " - " and " | ", so this is met, but real Yoast sites will produce untripped suffixes. Sprint 5 or later.
O. [PROCESS] Master Controller's amendments to the Sprint 4 and Sprint 5 files (reqs 12–14, connection pinning, team assignments) were committed inside Dev Team's code commit 08754c6. Substance is fine — they read as MC's and they're what the hash locks — but sprint-file changes riding in a code commit blur who changed what. Prefer MC commits its own amendments before Dev Team starts, or Dev Team leaves docs/sprints out of the code commit.

=== FOR PIPEMAN / LIVEQA ===
Per the sprint file, LiveQA's check is a boot + prior-screens smoke test; the comparison and title logic gets its live verification in Sprint 5 against the real results screen. Nothing in src/ or views/ changed this sprint.
